papers.title: Cycles upon cycles—Temperature scaling of medaka development
papers.system_description: Her7-mVenus medaka tail explants; batch1: 13–15 somites, batch2: 16–17 somites, with different media and imaging periods.
papers.tissue: Tail explant, including the PSM and tailbud.
papers.conditions: Constant 22/27/32°C; 21–27°C temperature cycles of 12 h/24 h (batch1) and 6 h (batch2, paired with the 27°C control). Cross-batch speed comparisons use the authors' correction.
papers.reporter_construct: CRISPR knock-in Her7-mVenus fusion reporter at the endogenous her7 locus; not a promoter-only transcriptional reporter.
papers.reported_target: Her7 protein fluorescence dynamics; phase estimated from intensity using wavelet or Hilbert analysis.
papers.figure_focus: Fig2C: intensity kymographs at 22/27/32°C; 2E: the same data with time rescaled by oscillation cycles. Fig3: phase SVD decomposition/reconstruction. Fig5A/B: cycling-temperature experiments; 5E/F: simulations.
papers.time_axis: Fig2C x-axis: 0–12 h; 2E x-axis: 0–6 cycles. TIFF columns represent time, with 10 min intervals for the 27°C sample; retain the absolute start time and crop window.
papers.space_axis: Fig2C/E: vertical axis, Space (µm), with 0 at the top and position increasing downward; TIFF rows represent space. Constant-temperature samples in batch1 use center-of-mass registration, so an anterior registration origin cannot be assumed.
papers.time_resolution: Methods: 10 min/frame; 5 min/frame at constant 32°C. The inspected 20200815 P1 data_settings also specifies 10 min. TIFF finterval=1 and XResolution are not physical time calibration.
papers.space_resolution: 512×512 images, 1.38µm/px; 5–10 z-planes at 7µm spacing; 20×/NA0.8. The inspected 27°C sample has data_settings dx=1.38µm.
papers.replicates: Paired intensity/phase data from 1 biological sample at 27°C were decoded. Fig5 reports replicates by condition; neither the number of files nor the two paired files was counted as biological n.
papers.preprocessing: Maximum z-projection, Gaussian σ4. One registration method: FIJI rigid-body center-of-mass registration, sampled along a 20px-wide polyline. Another: Ilastik mask → Matlab skeleton → transverse averaging along the midline and anterior registration. Batch1 uses wavelet analysis; the main text uses Hilbert analysis for batch2. SVD is applied to phase, not directly to raw intensity.
papers.summary: Temperature changes segmentation-clock speed while the spatial phase gradient remains relatively stable. Public intensity/phase kymographs and code support comparisons with the poster's waveforms, phase gradients and scaling relationships.

papers.title: Scaling of embryonic patterning based on phase-gradient encoding
papers.system_description: E10.5 mouse tailbud-derived quasi-monolayer PSM (mPSM); the control is cultured and imaged posterior embryo fragments containing PSM (called in vivo in the paper).
papers.conditions: Fibronectin substrate, 37°C, 5% CO₂; temperature control at 33°C. mPSM spreads initially and enters a clear segmentation phase after about 20 h.
papers.reporter_construct: LuVeLu: Lfng-regulated destabilized Venus fluorescent reporter (original construct: Aulehla2008); also a Mesp2-GFP targeted allele.
papers.reported_target: LuVeLu → Lfng / Notch-associated transcriptional activity; Mesp2-GFP → segmentation/differentiation marker. Neither directly represents gene-expression concentration without accounting for reporter dynamics.
papers.figure_focus: Fig4a: experimental kymograph and projection analysis used in the user's poster; 4b: experimental phase-gradient summary; 4c/d: numerical simulations. Fig1c: experimental embryonic PSM kymograph; Fig1f: experimental ex vivo mPSM kymograph, corresponding to Video 2. Fig3a is a segment width–mPSM length scatter plot, not a kymograph. Fig4a/b: experiments; 4c/d: simulations; Fig3d: schematic.
papers.time_axis: Fig1c/f: horizontal axis, Time (h), not video playback seconds.
papers.space_axis: Fig1c/f y-axis: Space (µm). c runs posterior→anterior; f runs centre→periphery, corresponding to posterior→anterior in mPSM.
papers.space_resolution: Original acquisition: 12-bit, 512×512, 1.38 µm/pixel; z-step 6–8 µm; 6–8 planes in embryos and 3–4 planes ex vivo.
papers.replicates: Fig1g period: embryo n=12, ex vivo n=16; Fig3a: 26 segments / 5 samples; Fig3b: 42 waves / 7 samples. Each n belongs to a different analysis.
papers.calibration_short: 10 min · video scale bar verified
papers.preprocessing: Maximum-intensity z projection; Gaussian smoothing at σ=7 px, followed by a center-to-edge line scan, further smoothing and saving as a text image. Detrending, moving average and a Hilbert transform at each spatial position yield phase. The MOV is a rendered supplementary video; retention of the original 12-bit intensities has not been established.
papers.summary: Experimental system cited in the poster: LuVeLu concentric traveling waves and segment scaling. Fig1f can serve as an experimental kymograph benchmark; the Video 2 file endpoint was verified as accessible.
papers.availability_summary: Official movies decoded · radial ROI re-extracted with tissue-centroid registration; raw imaging stacks not located.

papers.time_resolution: Fluorescence: 10 min/frame; simultaneous bioluminescence every 10 min (9 min exposure + 10 s LuVeLu). Burned-in times were read for all 155 Movie S2 frames: 0–25.69 h, displayed to 0.01 h. The time array is used rather than timing inferred from playback FPS.
papers.space_resolution: Laser scanning: 1.38 µm/pixel, 512×512, z-step 8 µm. Fig1 kymographs average along a 50 px ≈70 µm-wide line. Bioluminescence pixel scale is unverified. The Movie S2 redraw uses 100 µm/139 video pixels (≈0.719 µm/px), measured from the displayed scale bar; the original 1.38 µm pixel scale cannot be applied directly.
